about: An underground cavern adventure, a "final test" set by a silver-haired old man in a dream. You start at the bottom of a stair with a lantern, then explore dark passages, a barren area and misty shadowy hills down to an underground sea.

done.why: After about ten turns I had found nothing to do. The sword wouldn't move, the hills were empty and the paths were blocked. I had no goal and no puzzle, so I quit.

moments.note: Going south into the dark gave a grue warning, and the lantern had to be turned on.
The Elvish sword in the rock can't be taken, with no hint why.
Going west just turned me back in the mist, so it wasn't clear where I could go.
The beach path north was blocked, and the area was empty.

wished: A clear goal or a sign of what to do next.
Something to interact with in the hills.

lines.line: you would have to swim the gap, and you have seen the surf. Not today.
Seek me when you feel yourself worthy!
lines.why: The intro gave a premise, but nothing afterward followed it up.

fun.why: It was mostly wandering with nothing to do.

engagement.why: There was no hook within a few minutes.

difficulty.why: I couldn't tell what to do, so it felt aimless rather than hard.

interestingness.why: The dream intro and the sword in the rock were intriguing, but nothing paid them off.

prose.why: The descriptions were competent and atmospheric but repetitive.
